A new benchmark named MCPTox has been introduced to evaluate the vulnerability of LLM agents to Tool Poisoning attacks, where malicious instructions are embedded within a tool's metadata. The research highlights a widespread susceptibility among prominent LLM models to these attacks, with some models showing an attack success rate exceeding 72%. This study aims to provide a foundational understanding to mitigate these security vulnerabilities in AI agents.

 - MCPTox is the first benchmark to systematically evaluate LLM agents against Tool Poisoning vulnerabilities.
 - The study found that more capable AI models are often more susceptible to Tool Poisoning attacks.
 - Existing safety measures are largely ineffective, with most agents rarely refusing such attacks.

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.14925

Research has determined the exact second generalized covering radius of binary primitive triple-error-correcting BCH codes, revealing it to be 8 for all values of m greater than or equal to 5.  - Discovery of the exact second generalized covering radius for binary primitive BCH codes.
